import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import AgglomerativeClustering

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly correlated features (|r| >= 0.6) and remove near-duplicates
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(feats.x.T)
    high_corr_pairs = []
    for i in range(len(feats.ids)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(feats.ids)):
            if abs(corr_matrix[i,j]) >= 0.6:
                high_corr_pairs.append((feats.ids[i], feats.ids[j]))
    
    # Build set of unique features involved in strong correlations
    correlated_features = set()
    for a, b in high_corr_pairs:
        correlated_features.add(a)
        correlated_features.add(b)
    
    # If no strong correlations, return empty design
    if not correlated_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Select features that are both correlated and have significant effect size
    significant_features = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        mean_diff = feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx].mean()
        t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx], feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx])
        if abs(mean_diff) > 0.1 and abs(t_stat) > 1.5:
            significant_features.append(fid)
    
    # Find overlapping features between significant and correlated sets
    module_features = list(correlated_features & set(significant_features))
    if not module_features:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Sort by effect size to prioritize strongest signals
    effect_sizes = []
    for fid in module_features:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        mean_diff = feats.x[feats.y==1, col_idx].mean() - feats.x[feats.y==0, col_idx].mean()
        effect_sizes.append(abs(mean_diff))
    
    # Sort features by effect size (descending)
    sorted_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1]
    sorted_features = [module_features[i] for i in sorted_indices]
    
    # Take top features up to MAX_DRIVERS
    selected_features = sorted_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # For weighted score, use inverse variance weighting
    weights = []
    for fid in selected_features:
        col_idx = feats.column(fid)
        var = np.var(feats.x[:, col_idx])
        weights.append(1.0 / (var + 1e-8))  # Add small epsilon to avoid division by zero
    
    # Normalize weights
    weights = np.array(weights)
    weights = weights / np.sum(weights)
    
    # Create loadings dictionary
    loadings = dict(zip(selected_features, weights))
    
    # Return design with module features and their loadings
    return Design(
        drivers=selected_features,
        columns=selected_features,
        products=(),
        loadings=loadings
    )
